Published online:
    September 8, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (Nigeria, Middle East, Iran, Kenya, India)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references H1 profit, past losses, current capacity
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — persistent fuel shortages post-Iran war, inventory rebuilding
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — capacity doubling to 1.4m bpd by 2029, Kenya refinery, $14.3bn expansion, IPO

Synopsis:
    Dangote refinery's CEO states fuel shortages will persist well beyond the US-Iran war due to damaged Middle Eastern refining capacity, deferred maintenance, and the need to rebuild inventories. The refinery is capitalising on this environment — operating at full 700k bpd capacity and posting $1.82bn H1 profit after prior losses. An ambitious expansion to 1.4m bpd by 2029 is underway, funded partly by an IPO targeting ~$1.63bn. The macro backdrop of war-driven refining disruptions is framed as a structural, multi-year opportunity for Dangote.

Q01. Is the content's main message about EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
Relevance: NO — focus is on global refined product markets and African refining capacity, not EU/German energy specifically

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 45 — the general theme of war-driven refinery disruption is known; the specific forward-looking claim of prolonged multi-year shortages driven by inventory rebuilding and security stocking adds moderate incremental uncertainty
